title: MAVLink2 signing bypass: any message on MAVLINK_COMM_0 accepted unsigned, including non-USB transports

cvss_justification.AV: Adjacent — attacker must reach the SERIAL0-mapped physical transport (telemetry radio, network port, UART). Not pure Internet (AV:N) because vehicle is usually airgapped from public WAN, but on AP_Networking-enabled builds SERIAL0 can be a TCP/UDP socket.
cvss_justification.AC: L — no special timing, just send an unsigned MAVLink2 packet to COMM_0.
cvss_justification.PR: N — bypass deliberately requires no signature.
cvss_justification.C: H — attacker can read params, sensors, GPS via unsigned READ messages.
cvss_justification.I: H — attacker can call any handler reachable on COMM_0 (arm/disarm, mode change, mission upload, FTP, SERIAL_CONTROL, REBOOT_SHUTDOWN).
cvss_justification.A: H — REBOOT_SHUTDOWN, disarm in flight, switch to Land/RTL = vehicle crash.

source.description: accept_unsigned_callback invoked by mavlink_helpers.h for every received packet that lacks valid signature

sink.description: return true on COMM_0 status pointer, packet is then dispatched as authentic

taint_path.snippet: find_protocol_instance(SerialProtocol_MAVLink, instance) — instance 0 returns the FIRST SERIAL slot enabled for MAVLink, which can be a network or telemetry UART, not necessarily USB
chan = (mavlink_channel_t)(MAVLINK_COMM_0 + instance); — first MAVLink-enabled SERIAL becomes COMM_0
if (status == mavlink_get_channel_status(MAVLINK_COMM_0)) { return true; } — channel 0 is hardcoded as 'secure', allowing unsigned packets

reachability_evidence: GCS_MAVLINK::init (GCS_Common.cpp:143-157) maps chan=COMM_0+instance with instance pulled from find_protocol_instance order. On boards with AP_Networking (libraries/AP_Networking_port.cpp:126) a TCP/UDP MAVLink port can be the first MAVLink-protocol slot when SERIAL0 has been remapped (the boundary check at AP_SerialManager.cpp:442-444 only re-asserts state[0] is MAVLink2, not that state[0] is USB). Attackers reaching that link can bypass signing.
why_not_false_positive: The callback at line 117-122 returns true for COMM_0 without checking transport type; comment 'assumed to be secure channel. This is USB on ChibiOS boards' is an assumption that breaks on Linux/networking/non-USB boards. No build-time guard ties COMM_0 to USB.
survived_adversarial: Tried: argue COMM_0 is always USB on production firmware — REFUTED by AP_HAL_Linux/AP_HAL_ESP32/AP_Networking which support MAVLink-over-IP; the default for state[0] is MAVLink2 but the physical port assignment depends on hwdef and runtime SERIALn options. Tried: argue signing only matters once enabled — but the project ships signing as the official authentication mechanism for telemetry radios, so this exception silently neuters it on COMM_0.
preconditions: MAVLink2 signing has been set up on the vehicle (otherwise no signing at all)
Attacker can deliver bytes to the SERIAL slot that became COMM_0 (telemetry radio, network, debug UART)
attack_vector: Send any MAVLink2 packet WITHOUT a signature block to the physical channel mapped to MAVLINK_COMM_0; ArduPilot accepts as authentic and dispatches the contained command.
exploit_chain: 1. Identify the COMM_0 physical port (e.g. via SiK telemetry on Pixhawk USB-less builds or Ethernet on CubeOrange-Linux).
2. Forge an unsigned MAVLink2 COMMAND_LONG with MAV_CMD_COMPONENT_ARM_DISARM or MAV_CMD_PREFLIGHT_REBOOT_SHUTDOWN.
3. Transmit. accept_unsigned_callback returns true; handler executes.

poc.environment: SITL not available on Windows host
poc.expected_output: Vehicle disarms mid-flight despite signing being enabled

impact: Authentication bypass + remote control (arm/disarm/reboot/mode change) on ArduPilot vehicles with MAVLink2 signing nominally enabled
mitigation: Replace the 'COMM_0 is always trusted' rule with a per-channel trust attribute populated from hwdef and SerialManager (e.g. only set trust for ports whose UARTDriver reports usb_connected())
Or: remove the unconditional COMM_0 exception entirely and require signing on every channel

title: MAVFTP grants unauthenticated read/write/delete on the entire AP_Filesystem, including @SYS internals (signing keys, storage.bin)

cvss_justification.AV: A — reachable from any MAVLink transport (telemetry radio, network MAVLink, USB).
cvss_justification.AC: L — well-documented FTP protocol; pymavlink ships a client.
cvss_justification.PR: N — no auth check between the FTP dispatcher and the open()/write()/unlink() calls; MAVFTP relies on link-layer security alone, which is bypassed by finding aa13290d.
cvss_justification.C: H — read @SYS/storage.bin (StorageManager dump containing signing key blob, parameters), @SYS/flash.bin (entire firmware), arbitrary SD-card files including logs/scripts.
cvss_justification.I: H — write/overwrite arbitrary files: replace Lua scripts in APM/scripts/, mission files, parameter files. Combined with autoload, attacker code runs at next reboot.
cvss_justification.A: L — fill SD, delete logs; no immediate vehicle crash (but Lua replacement -> A:H in chain).

source.description: request.data populated from packet.payload[12..] — attacker-controlled MAVLink FILE_TRANSFER_PROTOCOL payload

sink.description: AP::FS().open((char *)request.data, O_RDONLY) — attacker-chosen path opened with no canonicalization or allow-list

taint_path.snippet: mavlink_msg_file_transfer_protocol_decode(&msg, &packet); request.data <- packet.payload[12..]
check_name_len(request) — only validates length, not content; no traversal/allow-list check
fd = AP::FS().open((char *)request.data, O_RDONLY); — opens via AP_Filesystem which routes @SYS/, @PARAM/, @MISSION/, @ROMFS/, or local SD path

if (strcmp(fname, "storage.bin") == 0) { ... hal.storage->get_storage_ptr(ptr, size); r.str->set_buffer((char*)ptr, size, size); } — exposes raw StorageManager region which contains MAVLink signing key and all params

reachability_evidence: handle_file_transfer_protocol (GCS_FTP.cpp:61) gates only on AP_BoardConfig::ftp_disabled() (default OFF on all flight controllers per FTP defaults). The Session::handle_request switch (lines 323-670) dispatches OpenFileRO/WriteFile/CreateFile/RemoveFile/RemoveDirectory/Rename without ever checking sysid, signing state, or operator role. AP_Filesystem_Sys exposes storage.bin which StorageManager uses to hold the MAVLINK2 signing key (libraries/GCS_MAVLink/GCS_Signing.cpp:29, StorageAccess::StorageKeys).
why_not_false_positive: GCS_FTP.cpp:323-670 has NO call to signing_enabled(), get_soft_armed(), or any operator-permission check before invoking AP::FS().open/write/unlink/rename. The signing-key region is reachable as @SYS/storage.bin even though documentation claims it's 'internal'.
survived_adversarial: Tried: maybe the FTP path is sanitized by AP_Filesystem::backend_by_path — REFUTED: that function only strips '@PREFIX/' to dispatch to a backend and otherwise passes the path through. Tried: maybe @SYS opendir is locked to read-only — TRUE (open at AP_Filesystem_Sys.cpp:71 rejects non-RDONLY), but read-only is sufficient to exfiltrate the signing key from storage.bin and own all future signed sessions. Tried: maybe flow control prevents bulk reads — REFUTED, BurstReadFile is supported.
preconditions: Attacker can deliver MAVLink FILE_TRANSFER_PROTOCOL frames (no signing OR finding aa13290d's COMM_0 bypass).
AP_MAVLINK_FTP_ENABLED is on (default true on most flight builds).
Optionally: SD card / FRAM populated with the assets the attacker cares about.
attack_vector: Send MAVLink FILE_TRANSFER_PROTOCOL OpenFileRO with payload = '@SYS/storage.bin' to extract the signing key, then write a Lua autoload script to /APM/scripts/persistent.lua.
exploit_chain: 1. Send FTP OpenFileRO with path '@SYS/storage.bin'.
2. Burst-read the StorageManager region. Locate the MAVLINK_SIGNING_KEY block (magic 0x3852fcd1) and extract the 32-byte secret_key.
3. Sign all future MAVLink2 packets with the stolen key — full impersonation.
4. (Optional) FTP CreateFile to /APM/scripts/backdoor.lua containing GCS-spoofing Lua and reboot.

poc.environment: SITL not available; reproducible via pymavlink's mftp module against any MAVFTP-enabled target
poc.payload: FILE_TRANSFER_PROTOCOL payload bytes 0..11 set opcode=OpenFileRO, path bytes 'storage.bin' under @SYS prefix
poc.expected_output: binary file containing signing key magic 0x3852fcd1 followed by 32-byte secret

impact: Information disclosure (signing key) + arbitrary file modification (Lua backdoor) on any ArduPilot vehicle with MAVFTP enabled
mitigation: Add an authorization layer in GCS_FTP::handle_file_transfer_protocol (or in handle_request) that rejects writes/deletes unless the link is signed or the sysid is on an allow-list
Make @SYS/storage.bin require a build flag and refuse to expose it over MAVFTP
Allow operators to set a permitted prefix (e.g. /APM/LOGS only) via a FTP_OPTIONS bitmask

title: DDS (XRCE) request handlers arm/disarm motors, switch flight mode, set parameters and trigger takeoff with no authentication

cvss_justification.AV: N — DDS uses UDP and the ArduPilot client connects to a Micro-XRCE-DDS-Agent. Any node on the DDS multicast domain (ROS_DOMAIN_ID, default 0) is a peer of the agent; on a flat L2/L3 path between agent and vehicle, an attacker on the same network can publish requests to the topic without binding to the FC.
cvss_justification.AC: L — XRCE-DDS sample messages are documented and ros2 CLI publishes them.
cvss_justification.PR: N — no DDS-layer auth (DDS-Security extension is not enabled); the handlers don't check requester identity.
cvss_justification.C: L — only response payloads are returned; main impact is integrity.
cvss_justification.I: H — arm motors, change flight mode, set arbitrary parameter, trigger VTOL takeoff.
cvss_justification.A: H — arming in flight, taking off remotely, switching to LAND mid-mission.

source.description: udp_transport_read receives untrusted bytes from XRCE agent connected via SocketAPM

sink.description: AP_DDS_External_Control::arm(AP_Arming::Method::DDS, do_checks) and similar invocations dispatched from on_request with no caller authentication

taint_path.snippet: const ssize_t ret = dds->udp.socket->recv(buf, len, timeout_ms); — bytes from network
void AP_DDS_Client::on_request(uxrSession* uxr_session, uxrObjectId object_id, ... ucdrBuffer* ub, ...) — dispatch entry
ardupilot_msgs_srv_ArmMotors_Request arm_motors_request; ... deserialize_topic(ub, &arm_motors_request);
arm_motors_response.result = arm_motors_request.arm ? AP_DDS_External_Control::arm(AP_Arming::Method::DDS, do_checks) : AP_DDS_External_Control::disarm(AP_Arming::Method::DDS, do_checks);
mode_switch_response.status = AP::vehicle()->set_mode(mode_switch_request.mode, ModeReason::DDS_COMMAND);
takeoff_response.status = AP::vehicle()->start_takeoff(takeoff_request.alt);
vp->set_and_save_by_name_ifchanged(param_key, param_value);

reachability_evidence: AP_DDS_Client::main_loop (line 1235) opens the UDP transport on AP_DDS_UDP.cpp:17 connecting to dds->udp.ip:dds->udp.port (defaults 0.0.0.0:2019 per var_info AP_GROUPINFO at AP_DDS_Client.cpp:140). on_request_trampoline (line 901) is registered via uxr_set_request_callback at line 1369. The on_request switch (line 911-1227) dispatches each service WITHOUT any identity, signing, or permission check on sample_id. The arm path explicitly passes do_checks=true (line 923) so prearm checks still run, BUT the operator does not have to be authorized.
why_not_false_positive: Grep for 'auth', 'permission', 'sysid' inside libraries/AP_DDS/ returns zero matches; the handlers consume the deserialized topic directly. DDS-Security (which would add cryptographic authentication) is not built into the ArduPilot XRCE bridge per AP_DDS_config.h. The do_checks=true on arm prevents some accidents but not motivated abuse — an attacker can wait until checks pass.
survived_adversarial: Tried: maybe the DDS UDP transport binds outbound-only and isn't reachable — TRUE for the immediate socket, BUT the XRCE-DDS Agent IS a network listener and any peer on the DDS domain reaches the FC handlers through it (which is the entire ROS 2 design intent and is documented). Tried: maybe prearm gates everything — REFUTED, set_parameters can adjust BRD_OPTIONS / ARMING_CHECK at runtime to defeat prearm.
preconditions: AP_DDS_ENABLED (built-in by default for SITL and many CubeOrange/Linux builds)
Vehicle reachable over the XRCE-DDS Agent's network (LAN, mesh radio, drone tether)
attack_vector: Publish an ArmMotors / ModeSwitch / Takeoff / SetParameters request on the ROS 2 DDS domain shared with the vehicle.
exploit_chain: 1. ros2 service call /ap/arm_motors ardupilot_msgs/srv/ArmMotors '{arm: true}' — vehicle arms.
2. ros2 service call /ap/mode_switch ardupilot_msgs/srv/ModeSwitch '{mode: 4}' — switches to GUIDED.
3. ros2 service call /ap/experimental/takeoff ardupilot_msgs/srv/Takeoff '{alt: 100}' — takes off.

poc.environment: Requires Micro-XRCE-DDS-Agent + ROS 2 on attacker host; SITL not available on Windows host
poc.expected_output: Vehicle ARMED (visible via MAVLink HEARTBEAT base_mode & MAV_MODE_FLAG_SAFETY_ARMED)

impact: Remote arming, takeoff, mode switch and arbitrary parameter modification on ROS 2-enabled ArduPilot vehicles
mitigation: Add DDS-Security (governance + permissions XML) so requesters must hold a CA-signed identity
Or: gate every on_request handler on a vehicle-side allow-list pulled from an authenticated config
Document DDS-without-security as 'physical-LAN only' in BIG letters in AP_DDS/README.md

title: Bootloader signature verification fail-open when all public keys are zero — first-boot configuration permits unsigned firmware

cvss_justification.AV: P — physical or near-physical access to push firmware via DFU/serial bootloader. Or remote if any earlier finding lets you remove keys (set_public_keys with zeroes).
cvss_justification.AC: L — flash firmware normally; if keys area is zero the unsigned firmware boots.
cvss_justification.PR: N — bootloader does not require authentication when no keys present.
cvss_justification.S: C — scope changes: bootloader (root-of-trust) accepting an attacker firmware compromises everything downstream including future signed boots.

sink.description: return check_fw_result_t::CHECK_FW_OK when all_zero_public_keys() AND unsigned firmware valid — allows boot of attacker-supplied unsigned image

taint_path.snippet: const struct ap_secure_data public_keys __attribute__((section(".apsec_data"))); — keys stored in bootloader sector, all-zero in factory state
static bool all_zero_public_keys(void) { ... return true; } — returns true if every slot is zero
if (all_zero_public_keys()) { return check_fw_result_t::CHECK_FW_OK; } — bypass in check_firmware_signature
const auto ret = check_good_firmware_signed(); if (ret != CHECK_FW_OK && all_zero_public_keys() && check_good_firmware_unsigned() == CHECK_FW_OK) return CHECK_FW_OK;

reachability_evidence: check_good_firmware (AP_CheckFirmware.cpp:175) is the bootloader entry. With AP_SIGNED_FIRMWARE, the code path at lines 181-187 explicitly says: if signed check fails AND all keys are zero, fall back to unsigned and return OK. The unsigned check (line 133-173) requires only CRC + board_id match, both attacker-controlled. Comment at line 178 says 'allow for use of SECURE_COMMAND to remove all public keys and then load of unsigned firmware' — the design lets the operator zero keys to disable signing. Combined with secure_command::set_public_keys (which can write zero arrays per AP_CheckFirmware_secure_command.cpp:357-381 REMOVE_PUBLIC_KEYS), a remote attacker who already has signing key can fully disarm the secure-boot chain.
why_not_false_positive: The branch is an intentional 'safety net' but it is also an attacker-useful fail-open. With the existence of REMOVE_PUBLIC_KEYS (which only requires a valid signature once), an attacker who steals the signing key can permanently zero keys and downgrade the device to unsigned, opening it to arbitrary firmware. Self-citing AP_CheckFirmware.cpp:177-187 and AP_CheckFirmware_secure_command.cpp:352-381.
survived_adversarial: Tried: argue 'set_public_keys requires a valid signature' — TRUE, but the failure mode chains with finding acbd74c9 (FTP extracts signing key from storage.bin) and finding aa13290d (COMM_0 unsigned bypass on Linux/network builds). Tried: argue 'an OEM ships with non-zero keys' — TRUE for some vendors, but ArduPilot's default reference image ships with zero keys until provisioned, so the fresh device is permanently downgradable.
preconditions: Either (a) device shipped with zero keys, or (b) attacker obtained signing key (see acbd74c9) and zeroed them via SECURE_COMMAND_SET_PUBLIC_KEYS
attack_vector: Flash an attacker-built unsigned firmware via DFU after zeroing keys.
exploit_chain: 1. Steal signing key via FTP @SYS/storage.bin (finding acbd74c9) or via factory image
2. Send SECURE_COMMAND_SET_PUBLIC_KEYS with all-zero payload to overwrite stored keys
3. Reboot and DFU-flash unsigned attacker firmware; bootloader accepts it

poc.environment: Requires hardware bootloader; not reproducible on Windows host
poc.payload: REMOVE_PUBLIC_KEYS for keys 0..9, then arbitrary unsigned firmware

impact: Permanent firmware-level compromise of any ArduPilot board with stolen signing key; ability to ship modified flight controllers undetected
mitigation: Remove the all_zero_public_keys() fallback in check_good_firmware_signed (lines 181-187). Operators who genuinely need to disable signing should reflash the bootloader.
If retained, require physical hardware strap (e.g. BOOT0 pin sequence) to confirm key wipe before accepting unsigned firmware

title: SECURE_COMMAND fail-open: any unsigned SECURE_COMMAND accepted when bootloader stores no public keys

cvss_justification.AV: A — reachable on every MAVLink transport.
cvss_justification.AC: L — send a SECURE_COMMAND with sig_length=64 of garbage; check_signature returns true if keys are zero.
cvss_justification.S: C — leads to bootloader-key tampering and firmware rollback (root of trust).
cvss_justification.H, A: H — attacker can set keys to attacker-controlled values, locking out legitimate operators.

source.description: handle_secure_command invoked with attacker-controlled mavlink_secure_command_t packet

sink.description: set_public_keys writes attacker-supplied keys into bootloader because check_signature returned true on zero-keys

taint_path.snippet: case MAVLINK_MSG_ID_SECURE_COMMAND: AP_CheckFirmware::handle_msg(chan, msg);
if (all_zero_keys(sec_data)) { return true; } — bypass inside check_signature
if (!check_signature(pkt)) { reply.result = MAV_RESULT_DENIED; goto send_reply; } — check_signature returned true, so DENIED is skipped
if (set_public_keys(key_idx, num_keys, &pkt.data[1])) { reply.result = MAV_RESULT_ACCEPTED; } — bootloader keys written from attacker payload

reachability_evidence: AP_CheckFirmware_secure_command.cpp:199 short-circuits check_signature when all keys are zero. handle_secure_command at line 281 gates only on this check. On a freshly provisioned ArduPilot board (or one whose keys were wiped by an OEM mistake) any MAVLink peer can send SECURE_COMMAND_SET_PUBLIC_KEYS to set attacker keys, then SECURE_COMMAND_GET_SESSION_KEY and so on.
why_not_false_positive: The comment at line 200 says 'allow through if no keys are setup' — intentional. The 'fail-open on missing keys' pattern is a known anti-pattern (CWE-305) because empty-key state is reachable through misconfiguration, factory-default, or REMOVE_PUBLIC_KEYS abuse.
survived_adversarial: Tried: argue zero-key state requires physical setup — REFUTED by the explicit fall-through in check_signed_bootloader (line 414-425) and check_signature (line 199) that document zero state as supported. Tried: argue once keys are set, the device is safe — TRUE, but the *transition* (factory default to provisioned) is unauthenticated.
preconditions: Public-key area in bootloader is all-zero (factory state OR after REMOVE_PUBLIC_KEYS)
attack_vector: Send a SECURE_COMMAND_SET_PUBLIC_KEYS with sig_length=64 of arbitrary bytes and 32-byte attacker public key; vehicle accepts, attacker now owns secure-boot.
exploit_chain: 1. Detect zero-keys state by sending SECURE_COMMAND_GET_PUBLIC_KEYS — receiving back an empty key set indicates fail-open
2. Send SECURE_COMMAND_SET_PUBLIC_KEYS with attacker pubkey; check_signature returns true (zero-keys bypass) and bootloader is updated
3. Now only the attacker can sign future commands; legitimate operator locked out

poc.environment: Requires hardware; SITL doesn't run secure_command
poc.payload: mavlink_secure_command_t with operation=SET_PUBLIC_KEYS, data=[key_idx=0]+[attacker_pubkey 32B], sig_length=64, signature=64xAA

impact: Bootkit-grade compromise: attacker installs own signing keys, then signs any future firmware/command. Legitimate owner cannot recover without physical reflash.
mitigation: Remove the all_zero_keys() bypass in check_signature
Require an out-of-band key-provisioning bootloader mode entered by physical strap
Refuse SECURE_COMMAND on links other than USB until at least one key is installed

title: DDS Joy topic allows unauthenticated RC channel override (steer/throttle hijack) from any DDS peer

cvss_justification.AV: N — DDS UDP/agent reachable from network.
cvss_justification.C: N — attacker only sets, doesn't read.
cvss_justification.I: H — overrides RC channels 0..7, which on Plane includes aileron/elevator/throttle/rudder.
cvss_justification.A: H — taking over flight controls in real time = vehicle crash.

sink.description: RC_Channels::set_override(i, mapped_data, t_now) called with attacker-supplied axes data

taint_path.snippet: const ssize_t ret = dds->udp.socket->recv(buf, len, timeout_ms);
const bool success = sensor_msgs_msg_Joy_deserialize_topic(ub, &rx_joy_topic);
const uint16_t mapped_data = static_cast<uint16_t>(linear_interpolate(rc().channel(i)->get_radio_min(), rc().channel(i)->get_radio_max(), rx_joy_topic.axes[i], -1.0, 1.0));
RC_Channels::set_override(i, mapped_data, t_now);

reachability_evidence: AP_DDS_JOY_SUB_ENABLED is on by default per AP_DDS_config.h when DDS is built. on_topic dispatcher at line 818 receives any Joy publish on the configured DDS topic and writes set_override for channels 0..7. There is no check on the publisher's identity, the vehicle's flight mode, or whether a stick-priority condition holds.
why_not_false_positive: set_override is the same primitive used by legitimate RC takeover; it bypasses the manual RC stick check until it times out. The handler does not consult rc().has_valid_input() or operator allow-list.
survived_adversarial: Tried: maybe the linear_interpolate clamps to safe range — TRUE for in-range axes, BUT attacker chooses the value within radio_min..radio_max, which is the full deflection range. Tried: maybe RC failsafe pre-empts — only after timeout; during the override the attacker is in full control.
preconditions: AP_DDS_ENABLED and AP_DDS_JOY_SUB_ENABLED (defaults on for DDS builds)
attack_vector: Publish sensor_msgs/Joy on the vehicle's joy topic via ros2 topic pub.
exploit_chain: 1. ros2 topic pub /ap/joy sensor_msgs/msg/Joy '{axes: [1.0, -1.0, 1.0, -1.0]}' — full deflection on AETR.
2. Vehicle's RC override flips controls; manual pilot stick is ignored until override times out (>1s).

poc.expected_output: Plane rolls hard right, pitches up, full throttle

impact: Real-time flight-control hijack of any ROS 2-bridged ArduPilot vehicle
mitigation: Gate Joy override behind a runtime-configurable allow-list or DDS-Security identity
Add a DDS_OPTIONS bit to require an explicit operator opt-in before Joy override is honored
Honor STICK_MIXING / RC stick-priority parameters before applying set_override

title: SERIAL_CONTROL passthrough lets any MAVLink peer drive arbitrary onboard UART at chosen baudrate (GPS, ESC, IO MCU)

cvss_justification.AC: L — well-known protocol used by uploader.py.
cvss_justification.PR: N — no auth check in handler.
cvss_justification.S: C — escapes MAVLink scope into raw UART traffic to peripherals (GPS, ESC, IO MCU).
cvss_justification.C: H — read GPS NMEA, ESC telemetry, IO firmware.
cvss_justification.I: H — write to IO MCU bootloader / spoof GPS to peripheral.
cvss_justification.A: H — bricking peripherals or driving wrong inputs to flight control.

source.description: mavlink_serial_control_t packet decoded from attacker MAVLink frame

sink.description: stream->write(packet.data, packet.count) — raw bytes piped to selected UART

taint_path.snippet: mavlink_msg_serial_control_decode(&msg, &packet); — attacker chooses device, baudrate, data

2. OR target IOMCU UART with bootloader entry sequence and reflash IOMCU

mitigation: Disable SERIAL_CONTROL by default and require a build flag for vendor diagnostic builds

title: AP_Filesystem_Sys exposes raw StorageManager dump (storage.bin) including MAVLink signing key

cvss_justification.S: C — leaks the secret used to authenticate to a different scope (signing).

sink.description: r.str->set_buffer((char*)ptr, size, size); — exposes the StorageManager region (which holds signing key)

taint_path.snippet: if (strcmp(fname, "storage.bin") == 0) {
if (hal.storage->get_storage_ptr(ptr, size)) { r.str->set_buffer((char*)ptr, size, size); }
StorageAccess GCS_MAVLINK::_signing_storage(StorageManager::StorageKeys); — signing key lives in this storage region readable via storage.bin

why_not_false_positive: hal.storage->get_storage_ptr returns the whole storage region; there is no per-section ACL. StorageManager::StorageKeys is within it. Files in @SYS are routed to AP_Filesystem_Sys::open which directly exposes the pointer.
survived_adversarial: Tried: argue storage.bin is excluded from FTP by some allowlist — REFUTED, no allowlist in GCS_FTP::handle_request; only @SYS write is rejected (open at 71 enforces RDONLY), but read passes.
exploit_chain: 1. mavftp> get @SYS/storage.bin storage.bin
2. python -c "d=open('storage.bin','rb').read(); ofs=d.find(b'\xd1\xfc\x52\x38'); print(d[ofs+12:ofs+44].hex())" — print signing key
3. Use the key to sign attacker MAVLink2 packets

poc.expected_output: Binary blob containing SIGNING_KEY_MAGIC 0x3852fcd1 + secret_key bytes

impact: Disclosure of the MAVLink2 signing key (32-byte ed25519-style secret), permitting full impersonation of the legitimate GCS
mitigation: Filter @SYS file names by a reportable list that excludes storage.bin/flash.bin
Encrypt-at-rest for StorageManager::StorageKeys
Make MAVFTP refuse @SYS by default unless a debug parameter is set
